title: Restocking Price Basis for Lines Reduced After List Price
content:
On a Returns & Exchanges return, the restocking percentage on a grade B unit is charged on the line's restocking price basis. The basis is set by what was taken off the line after its list price, so that a reduction granted after the list price does not lower the restocking charge.

## Restocking price basis

| What the Online Orders records show on the line | Restocking price basis per unit |
|---|---|
| A price adjustment | The merchandise credit per accepted unit plus the price adjustment per unit booked |
| No price adjustment, but a checkout promotion discount or a late promotion credit | The merchandise credit per accepted unit plus those reductions per unit booked (the checkout promotion discount allocated to the line and any late promotion credits, together) |
| No price adjustment, no checkout promotion discount and no late promotion credit | The merchandise credit per accepted unit |

- **Merchandise credit per accepted unit:** the merchandise part of the line's credit entry divided by the line's accepted units.
- **Price adjustment per unit booked:** the total of the price adjustments on the line divided by the units booked on the line.
- A line carrying a price adjustment adds back the price adjustment only; its promotions are not added as well.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

A line booked with 2 units has a merchandise credit per accepted unit of 72.00.

| Line history | Basis |
|---|---|
| Price adjustments totalling 10.00 | 72.00 plus 10.00 divided by 2, that is 77.00 |
| Checkout promotion discount of 16.00, no adjustment | 72.00 plus 16.00 divided by 2, that is 80.00 |
| Checkout promotion discount of 10.00 and a late promotion credit of 6.00, no adjustment | 72.00 plus 16.00 divided by 2, that is 80.00 |
| Price adjustment of 10.00 and a checkout promotion discount of 16.00 | 72.00 plus 10.00 divided by 2, that is 77.00 |
| No reductions | 72.00 |
